# Spotify Project

Authors: [Bernacchia Alessia](https://github.com/AlessiaBernacchia), [Pioda Tommaso](https://github.com/Thetommigun432), [Villani Giacomo](https://github.com/DownToTheGround)

```{r}
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(tidymodels)
library(vip)
library(ggcorrplot)
library(caret)


billboard <- read_csv("billboard.csv",
                           col_types = cols(url = col_skip(),
                            song = col_skip(), song = col_skip(),
                            previous_week_position = col_skip(),
                            performer = col_skip(),
                            weeks_on_chart = col_skip(),
                            peak_position = col_skip(),
                            instance = col_skip()
                            ))

audio_features <- read_csv("audio_features.csv", 
                           col_types = cols( 
                            performer = col_skip(), song = col_skip(), 
                            spotify_track_preview_url = col_skip(),
                            spotify_track_explicit = col_skip(),
                            spotify_track_album = col_skip(),
                            spotify_track_album = col_skip(),
                            spotify_track_id = col_skip()
                            ))

billboard <- billboard %>%
  group_by(song_id) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_week_position = round(mean(week_position, na.rm = TRUE), 0),
    week_id = n()
  )

print(head(audio_features,10))
```

```{r}
#audio_features <- na.omit(audio_features) # remove all NaN

# Step 1: Rimuovi caratteri indesiderati
audio_features$spotify_genre <- gsub("\\[|\\]|'", "", audio_features$spotify_genre)

# Step 2: Creare una lista di generi separati da virgola
audio_features$spotify_genre <- strsplit(audio_features$spotify_genre, split = ",")

# Step 3: Estrarre solo il primo genere per ogni riga
audio_features$first_genre <- sapply(audio_features$spotify_genre, function(x) x[1])

audio_features$first_genre <- sapply(audio_features$spotify_genre, function(x) {
  if (length(x) == 0) {
    return("others")
  } else {
    return(x[1])
  }
})

# Conta la frequenza di ciascun valore nella colonna 'first_genre'
genre_counts <- table(audio_features$first_genre)

# Identifica i generi con meno di 50 occorrenze
low_count_genres <- names(genre_counts[genre_counts < 200])

# Sostituisci i generi con meno di 50 occorrenze con "others"
audio_features$first_genre <- ifelse(audio_features$first_genre %in% low_count_genres, "others", audio_features$first_genre)

# Ricontrolla le frequenze dopo il raggruppamento
genre_counts_after_grouping <- table(audio_features$first_genre)
audio_features <- subset(audio_features, select = -c(spotify_genre))


# 1. Assicurati di usare la colonna aggiornata
df <- data.frame(first_genre = audio_features$first_genre)

# 2. Crea i dummy variables (one-hot encoding)
dummy <- dummyVars(~ first_genre, data = df)
final_df <- data.frame(predict(dummy, newdata = df))  # <- Qui dovevi usare final_df

# 3. Unisci con il dataset originale
audio_features_encoded <- bind_cols(
  audio_features %>% select(-first_genre),
  final_df
)

audio_features <- na.omit(audio_features)


full_data <- left_join(billboard, audio_features, by = "song_id") #merge datasets

#full_data$previous_week_position[is.na(full_data$previous_week_position)] <- 0

#create the new variable top10: whether a song is in the top 10
full_data_clean <- full_data %>%
  filter(!is.na(spotify_track_popularity)) 

full_data_clean <- full_data_clean %>%
  mutate(top10 = ifelse(mean_week_position <= 30, 1, 0))


full_data_clean <- full_data_clean %>% select(-c(song_id, mean_week_position))

full_data_clean$spotify_track_popularity <- sapply(full_data_clean$spotify_track_popularity, function(x) {
  if (x <= 25) {
    return("low")
  }
  if (x > 25 & x <= 50) {
    return("medium")
  }
  if (x > 50 & x <= 75) {
    return("high")
  }
    if (x > 75 & x <= 100) {
    return("very high")
  } 
})

print(colSums(is.na(full_data_clean)))
```

```{r}
# select only numerical data
numeric_data <- full_data_clean %>%
  select(where(is.numeric))

# correlation matrix
cor_matrix <- cor(numeric_data, use = "complete.obs")

ggcorrplot(cor_matrix, 
           method = "square",      # or "circle"
           type = "lower",         # only lower triangle        
           colors = c("red", "white", "blue"),  # come in seaborn
           title = "Correlation Matrix",
           ggtheme = ggplot2::theme_minimal())
```

```{r}
set.seed(42)
full_data_clean$top10 <- as.factor(full_data_clean$top10)
spotify_train_test <- full_data_clean |> initial_split(prop =  0.7)
spotify_train <- training(spotify_train_test); 
spotify_test  <- testing(spotify_train_test)
```

```{r}
rand_forest_spec <- 
  rand_forest(mtry = 5, trees = 200) |>  
  set_engine('randomForest') |> 
  set_mode('classification')

rf_recipe = recipe(top10~.,
                   data=spotify_train)

rf_wf <- workflow() |> 
  add_recipe(rf_recipe) |> 
  add_model(rand_forest_spec)

rf_wf_fit <- rf_wf |> 
  fit(spotify_train)

rf_wf_fit
```

```{r}
spotify_test_rf <- rf_wf_fit |> 
  augment(spotify_test)

cm_rF <- spotify_test_rf |> 
  conf_mat(truth=top10,
           estimate=.pred_class)
cm_rF
```

```{r}
head(summary(cm_rF),4)
```

```{r}
roc_rF<-roc_curve(spotify_test_rf,
          top10,
          .pred_0,event_level = "first")
roc_rF |> autoplot()
```
